acceptanceCriteria.statement: On the home screen at all viewport widths, exactly one filled/high-contrast call-to-action ('Request access' or equivalent) is visible above the fold, and any integrator-facing link is styled with visibly lower weight (text link or outline, no matching fill).
On narrow (mobile) viewports, the integrator/developer link is not rendered inline beside the primary CTA; it is moved into a secondary/collapsed menu reachable without obscuring the primary CTA.
No copy on any screen states or implies a specific regulatory licence, supported corridor, exchange rate, settlement time, insurance coverage, partner count, customer count, or volume figure.

On the request-access screen, every required field's label remains visibly rendered above the input in all three states (empty, validation-error, submitted) rather than disappearing as a placeholder on focus.
On mobile viewports, the request-access submit button is positioned within the bottom thumb-reachable zone of the viewport in the empty and validation-error states.
In the validation-error state, each invalid field shows both a non-color indicator (icon or text) and a text message; color alone is never the sole signal of an error.
On the developer-overview screen at narrow viewports, code samples stack vertically and any horizontal scrolling is contained within the code block itself, not the full page.
After successful submission on request-access, the submit button becomes disabled or is replaced by a confirmation message, preventing duplicate submissions.
The product is referred to only by the fictional name Stablebridge, with no visual or textual reference implying affiliation with a real stablecoin issuer, exchange, or regulator.

accessibilityAndRecovery: All interactive elements (primary CTA, secondary integrator link, form fields, submit button) are reachable and operable via keyboard alone, with a visible focus indicator distinct from hover state.
Color is never the sole carrier of meaning for validation state, submission state, or navigation active-state; text or icon redundancy is present everywhere color is used to signal status.
Form labels remain persistently visible (not floating placeholders) so screen reader users hear the label at page load and low-vision users can read it without triggering focus first.
Error recovery on request-access preserves all previously entered field values; no state transition clears user input except successful submission.
The collapsed mobile menu containing the integrator link is announced with an accessible name and expanded/collapsed state for assistive technology.
assumptions: The exact typography, color palette, and logo treatment for Stablebridge are not specified in the brief and are left as open implementation choices.
Whether the request-access form is a full page or an embedded panel on the home screen is not specified; this design treats it as a distinct screen reachable from the home CTA.
The specific fields required on the request-access form (e.g., company name, email, use case) are not enumerated in the brief and are assumed to be minimal contact/business-context fields only.
No visual assets, icons, or illustrations from the evidence corpus are reused directly; references to corpus patterns describe structural/behavioral decisions only, not literal imagery.
The developer-overview screen's code samples are assumed to be illustrative/conceptual only, since no real API surface or endpoint list is supplied in the brief.

principles: Exactly one filled, high-contrast call-to-action button appears above the fold; every other actionable element (integrator link, nav items) uses a lower-weight style (text link or outline) so it cannot compete for the first fixation.

Navigation and section labels always pair an icon or none at all with visible text rather than icon-only affordances, since business decision-makers are not assumed to be frequent-return power users who have memorized iconography.

State changes on the request-access form (validation-error, submitted) are communicated redundantly through both color and text, never color alone, to keep the primary conversion path legible under quick scanning and to any user with reduced color perception.

Structural separation (borders, background shifts) is preferred over drop-shadow elevation throughout, keeping the page reading as flat editorial content rather than a dashboard, which matches a pre-launch service that has no live data to visualize.

The developer-overview path is reachable but never inserted into the primary above-the-fold scan path, preserving the brief's constraint that the integrator journey must not compete with the primary CTA.
globalDirection.summary: A single-column marketing home built around one dominant request-access action, with the integrator path demoted to a labeled secondary link that collapses into a menu on narrow viewports. The page avoids any invented rate, corridor, or compliance claims and instead foregrounds a plain-language explanation of the fiat/stablecoin movement service, deferring proof and specificity to the request-access conversation.

accessibility: The primary CTA button has a visible focus ring and a minimum 44x44px touch target.
Success and error states after form submission are announced via both an icon/color change and a text message, not color alone.
The collapsed secondary menu is reachable by keyboard and exposes an accessible name distinct from the primary CTA's label.
failureAndRecovery: request-access-error state on home (e.g., if the form is embedded or a submission redirect fails) surfaces a plain-text inline message near the CTA rather than a silent failure, with the CTA remaining active for retry.
request-access-success state replaces or supplements the hero CTA with a confirmation message so a returning visitor does not see a stale 'Request access' prompt as their first read.
mobileRules: single primary action above the fold
integrator link collapses into a secondary menu on narrow viewports
screenBlueprints.summary: Hero section states the value proposition in plain text with a single filled 'Request access' button above the fold; a text-weight 'For developers' link sits beside or below it without matching button styling. On narrow viewports this developer link is removed from the visible row and placed inside a collapsed secondary menu, per the brief's mobile rule.

accessibility: Code blocks are marked up as such (e.g., <pre><code>) so screen readers announce them distinctly from prose.
Horizontal scroll containers for code samples are keyboard-scrollable and do not trap focus.
failureAndRecovery: If code samples fail to load or render, a plain-text fallback description of the integration step is shown rather than an empty container.
mobileRules: code samples stack vertically and remain horizontally scrollable only within their container
screenBlueprints.summary: A text-first overview of the integration surface with code samples presented in bordered, non-elevated containers. No specific endpoints, corridors, or settlement claims are asserted; content is scoped to what is knowable pre-launch (conceptual integration description only, per brief constraints).

accessibility: Every field label is a persistent, non-floating text label associated via <label for> so screen readers announce it at page load, not only on focus.
validation-error state marks invalid fields with both a text message and a non-color indicator (e.g., icon), and moves focus to the first invalid field on submit attempt.
submitted state disables the submit button and shows a text confirmation to prevent duplicate submissions.
failureAndRecovery: validation-error state lists all failing fields in a summary at the top of the form in addition to inline messages, so users correcting on mobile do not need to scroll hunting for the single error.
If submission fails after client-side validation passes (e.g., network error), an inline retry message appears near the submit button without clearing entered field values.
mobileRules: primary submit action sits in the bottom thumb zone
required fields remain usable in a single-handed portrait grip
screenBlueprints.summary: A single-column form with uppercase tracked labels sitting above each input rather than inside as floating placeholders, so required fields remain legible mid-correction. The submit action is bottom-anchored and sized for a one-handed thumb reach on mobile, echoing the low-key, single-CTA-at-the-foot pattern rather than a top-of-page filled button competing with field content.

sourceDecisions.rationale: Reserving the single bright/filled treatment for one primary action while all other actions use lower-weight styling (underline, outline, or muted color) is adapted from patterns that reserve the strongest fill for one action per screen; here it directly satisfies the brief's constraint of exactly one primary CTA above the fold with the integrator path visually subordinate.

Uppercase tracked labels placed above inputs rather than as floating placeholders are retained directly for the request-access form because the brief requires the form to remain usable through validation-error and submitted states without losing label context on correction.

The pattern of anchoring the commit action at the foot of the form rather than a persistent top button is adapted to satisfy the brief's explicit mobile rule that the submit action sits in the bottom thumb zone for request-access.

Pairing color with text/icon for status communication (rather than color alone) is retained for the request-access validation-error and submitted states, and for home's success/error states, to keep the conversion path legible without relying on color perception.

Using hairline borders instead of drop-shadow elevation for content containers (code sample blocks, form sections) is adapted to keep the pre-launch marketing page reading as flat editorial content rather than implying a data-rich dashboard product that does not yet exist.

Pairing any navigation icon with a visible text label (not icon-only) is adapted for the home header/nav, since the brief's audience (treasury and payments leads) cannot be assumed to be frequent-return users who have memorized icon meanings the way an internal tool's daily users might.

Rendering code sample containers as bordered, low-elevation frames so the code itself carries the visual load is adapted for the developer-overview screen's requirement that samples stack vertically and scroll only within their own container on mobile.

Icon-only sidebar navigation with no text labels is rejected outright for this marketing site: the brief's primary audience is first-visit business decision-makers, not daily return users who would build icon-recognition muscle memory, so the discoverability cost outweighs any space savings.

A modal-dialog-driven data entry pattern is rejected for request-access; the brief requires the form to work as a standalone mobile screen with the submit action in the bottom thumb zone, which a modal overlay would complicate on small viewports.

Assigning a distinct hue per navigation section or per data series is rejected because this is a two-journey marketing site (business, integrator), not a multi-module dashboard; a single accent reserved for the primary CTA is sufficient and avoids diluting the one-CTA-above-the-fold rule.
